title: POC Sprint 3 lab results & tuning sync - Arborwell
summary: Sprint 3 results review: Redwood runtime outperforms Arborwell's incumbent in 95th percentile latency on short chat flows but trails on sustained throughput with larger batches. SE recommended tuning KV cache TTLs, lowering max_batch_size for tail-latency sensitive routes, and switching to int8 quantized variant for throughput tests. Next steps: Redwood to provision a 24h dedicated slot for a live throughput run vs incumbent, send updated pricing and security addendum, customer to provide production prompt set and peak traffic profile.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-07 15:30 UTC | Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Clara Nguyen (Redwood AE), Ethan Morales (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM), Samir Patel (CTO - Arborwell), Lori Blake (Head of MLOps), Diego Ruiz (SRE), Marta Silva (PM)

Summary (auto): We walked through sprint 3 lab benchmarks comparing Redwood and Arborwell's incumbent provider, focused on latency P50/P95/P99 and sustained throughput. Discussed tuning knobs and next steps to run a longer throughput replay on a dedicated slot. Security and procurement checkpoints briefly covered.

[00:00] Clara Nguyen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we did a quick slide run and then Ethan will walk through the lab numbers. How's everyone doing?
[00:18] Samir Patel: Good thanks, coming out of back-to-back with engineering but ready.
[00:22] Ethan Morales: cool, i'll share my screen, um okay looks like the sprint 3 artifact sheet, so first slide is latency microbench for the short chat flow you gave us, 8 token prompts ~ median 40 tokens.
[00:38] Lori Blake: quick note — we care about 95th for user facing chat, 99th only for background jobs.
[00:46] Ethan Morales: noted, ok so for the short chat flow Redwood's 95th is 150ms, incumbent AICloudX came in at 220ms under same concurrency, so ~30% improvement on tail.
[00:58] Diego Ruiz: uh is that with or without KV cache?
[01:00] Ethan Morales: that number is with prefix KV cache enabled and small batch size (max_batch_size=8), yes.
[01:06] Samir Patel: the throughput numbers though? Our concern is at peak, the incumbent handles sustained 12k rps with batching and 99ms p50 but higher p95.
[01:16] Ethan Morales: right — in our lab when we pushed sustained loads Redwood hit similar p50 but above 6k rps we started seeing queueing and tail latency climb, that's with default batching.
[01:28] Clara Nguyen: to be clear, the lab config was on shared test cluster; we can run a 24-hour dedicated slot with your traffic replay to reproduce the 12k rps scenario.
[01:38] Marta Silva: that is critical. We need real traffic shape, not synthetic ramp.
[01:42] Ethan Morales: agreed, replay will show burstiness effects. Also, we saw that enabling int8 quantized model for the throughput path improved tokens/s by ~1.8x with small increase in rouge-ish quality metrics — probably acceptable for your non-critical scoring routes.
[01:58] Lori Blake: hmm quality delta? did you run our eval set?
[02:02] Ethan Morales: yes, we ran your 300-prompt eval set — int8 had a 0.4% drop on exact-match style checks and negligible change in rouge for generative outputs. I can share the spreadsheet.
[02:12] Samir Patel: send that. If quality holds, we'd be comfortable using quantized model on the high-throughput path and FP16 for low-latency interactive paths.
[02:20] Diego Ruiz: what's the effort to switch routes? Are we talking model variants per route or per deployment?
[02:26] Ethan Morales: Redwood supports per-route model variants and smart routing rules. You can pin low-latency routes to fp16 and route bulk classification and ingestion to int8 quantized instances.
[02:36] Clara Nguyen: also worth noting the runtime supports KV cache TTL tuning — the cache hit rate in your profile was 42% with a 30s TTL; extending TTL to 90s bumps hits to ~62% in the lab which reduces per-request compute and tail-latency.
[02:50] Marta Silva: any concerns with cached sensitive content? Our legal team is strict on PII.
[02:54] Priya Rao: quick interject — we have customer-controlled KV encryption options and support KMS-backed keys in Private deployments; for hosted we can enable token-level redaction and configurable retention. I'll attach the security doc.
[03:08] Lori Blake: good. Also SOC2 is a must for us.
[03:12] Clara Nguyen: Redwood is SOC2 Type II — Priya will share the cert.
[03:16] Diego Ruiz: back to throughput — you mentioned queueing, are we hitting GPU memory limits or just batching effects?
[03:22] Ethan Morales: a mix — with default kernel selection at longer sequences the memory and compute per request increases; sustained high concurrency pushes worker queue depth up. Reducing max_batch_size to 16 and increasing worker instances in dedicated slot kept tail stable to higher RPS.
[03:36] Samir Patel: why not increase batch size then? Larger batch = higher throughput, right?
[03:40] Ethan Morales: yes, but larger batches increase tail latency for short requests because requests wait to fill the batch. That's the classic latency vs throughput tradeoff. Smart routing and continuous batching help, but for user-facing chat we recommend smaller batches.
[03:54] Marta Silva: can you modify the batching policy per route?
[03:57] Ethan Morales: yes, batching policy is per-route with target latency thresholds — we can set latency SLOs so the router prioritizes low-latency execution for those routes while pushing bulk tasks to throughput-optimized pools.
[04:08] Lori Blake: ok, the architecture team wants details of the fallback behavior if our dedicated capacity is saturated.
[04:14] Clara Nguyen: Redwood supports fallback policies — route-level fallback to a cheaper model variant or to the hosted shared pool. We can set concurrency limits and automatic throttling. We'll include an example configuration.
[04:26] Samir Patel: procurement will ask about cost for the 24h dedicated run — will that be free or billable?
[04:32] Clara Nguyen: by default it's billable but we can treat the first 24h as a sponsored benchmark if we agree on scheduling and scope; we'll reflect that in the pricing note.
[04:42] Diego Ruiz: in your tests you mentioned model kernel selection — any special hardware dependencies?
[04:46] Ethan Morales: our runtime picks kernels based on architecture; for quantized paths we optimized kernels for Ampere and the newer H100 like families. We'll note the hardware used in the lab kit so you can correlate to your cloud instance types.
[05:00] Marta Silva: please put the hardware table into the report.
[05:03] Ethan Morales: will do.
[05:05] [05:05] Clara Nguyen: quick pause, Priya, did you get the procurement checklist updated?
[05:09] Priya Rao: yes, I updated the checklist in the shared drive — includes SOC2, SSO/SAML integration steps, audit log retention options, and KMS/HSM integration details.
[05:20] Lori Blake: SSO is key — we need SAML support and SCIM for user provisioning.
[05:24] Priya Rao: supported, and we can walk through the SSO plan in the next security call.
[05:29] Samir Patel: what's the path if we want a private deployment in our VPC? We likely prefer that for PHI workloads.
[05:34] Clara Nguyen: Private deployment is available — it's a separate engagement and licensing, includes customer-managed VPC, optional on-prem packages and HSM/KMS integration. We'll include a rough TCO estimate.
[05:44] Marta Silva: we'll need that TCO to compare to incumbent.
[05:47] Ethan Morales: to summarize the tuning recommendations from the lab: 1) run quantized int8 for bulk routes, 2) reduce max_batch_size for low-latency routes, 3) increase KV cache TTL for high hit-rate flows, 4) run dedicated slot for a replay test to validate 12k rps sustained.
[06:05] Diego Ruiz: for the dedicated slot test, can we bring our own request generator or do you prefer to run it?
[06:11] Ethan Morales: you can bring the generator or provide the trace and we'll run it in our lab; if you run it in your env we can provide the same worker config to reproduce.
[06:18] Clara Nguyen: ok next steps — we will provision the slot and share timeline. Any other blockers?
[06:24] Marta Silva: procurement sign-off and legal review of the security addendum.
[06:28] Priya Rao: I already added legal contacts to the shared folder.
[06:32] Samir Patel: one more question — how will you measure cost per 1M tokens in dedicated vs hosted?
[06:37] Clara Nguyen: we'll include per-token estimates broken down by route, including batching and cache effects. That will be in the pricing spreadsheet.
[06:46] Ethan Morales: also, small gotcha — the incumber's metric was reported with aggressive request coalescing at the edge; we can simulate that too but their latencies might be optimistic in some scenarios.
[06:58] Diego Ruiz: understood.
[07:00] [wrap-up]
[07:00] Clara Nguyen: good meeting — recap of next steps and action items posted. We'll follow up with scheduling for the dedicated run and the security docs. Thanks everyone.
[07:10] Samir Patel: thanks, appreciate it.
[07:12] Marta Silva: thanks all.
